A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same hierarchical uncertainty framework. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and can be matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original registration experiments on ABIDE and OASIS3, uncertainty-error correlations, ablations and qualitative downstream segmentation results.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds controlled registration experiments in Appendix D, Tables 8–9.

M1.justification: The proposed network, losses, uncertainty hierarchy and transformation-fitting procedures in Section 3 remain unchanged. Appendix D tests alternative training configurations as diagnostic ablations rather than replacing or extending the proposed framework.

E1.justification: Both versions train on HCP and ADNI and evaluate atlas registration on ABIDE and OASIS3. The added experiments change training configurations within this coverage, without introducing datasets, populations or tasks.

E2.justification: The RbR comparison in Table 2 and existing transformation and uncertainty comparisons are retained. Appendix D reuses weighted versus unweighted fitting controls under alternative training configurations; the newly cited studies are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix D adds weighted/unweighted fitting experiments with B-spline-based training and direct-coordinate interpolation in the training segmentation loss. Existing splits, preprocessing, metrics and test samples remain unchanged. The newly reported training duration and quality-control information document settings rather than establish revisions to existing experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds two targeted tests of whether using a transformation during training limits the benefit of uncertainty weighting at inference. The coordinate-loss and training-transform ablations in Tables 6–7 are retained and moved to Appendix C, not newly added.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same mean-plus/minus reporting and identify significant differences using a t-test at p = 0.05. The added tables follow this practice; no new seed counts, repeated-run protocol, confidence intervals or statistical estimation procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 retain their values. New Table 8 reports nearly identical unweighted/weighted B-spline results: 0.710/0.710 on ABIDE and 0.699/0.700 on OASIS3. Table 9 reports Demons results after direct-deformation training of 0.767/0.799 and 0.759/0.783, respectively. These are additional condition-specific comparisons, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The Gaussian assumptions, weighted least-squares formulation, covariance propagation, smoothing formulas and sampling expressions remain unchanged. The new appendices introduce empirical analyses and computational details, without new mathematical definitions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about hierarchical uncertainty propagation, stronger error correlation for aleatoric uncertainty, improved registration through weighted fitting and downstream uncertainty sampling.

C2.justification: Appendix D supports the earlier explanation for Demons' negligible weighting benefit and adds the interpretation that uncertainty helps fitting generalize across transformation models. Appendix E identifies B-spline matrix inversion as the main runtime bottleneck. The existing limitations remain unchanged, moving from Appendix C to F.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly documents visual quality control of NiftyReg reference registrations, with none excluded. Appendix E adds an NVIDIA RTX A6000, approximately 1.2 hours per epoch, typical convergence after 50 epochs and approximately 15 minutes per scan for prediction and all fitting variants. Existing architecture, hyperparameters and access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Chen et al.'s registration survey and Zhang et al.'s heteroscedastic uncertainty work. Section 2 distinguishes Zhang's aleatoric loss from this paper's propagation to transformation models and downstream tasks; the broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 expands introductory motivation and related-work discussion, adds acknowledgments, updates affiliation and publication-header text, and moves two ablation discussions into Appendix C. These are localized edits and organizational changes rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 8–9, relocates Tables 6–7 and rearranges existing figures, including swapping the numbering of Figures 3 and 4. Figure 2 gains abbreviated labels and explicit units. The six figures retain their underlying images.

improvement.justification: Appendix D provides targeted empirical support for Section 4.3's previously speculative explanation of the Demons result. Added quality-control and computational-cost disclosures improve transparency. These are useful, limited gains: the main method and existing results remain stable, and downstream usefulness still lacks quantitative validation.
